# Generated Files

The directory `lib/src/rust/` contains files generated by
**`uniffi-bindgen-dart` (0.1.x)** from the UniFFI FFI crate (`frf-ffi`). Do not edit these
files by hand.

> **Why not flutter_rust_bridge?** `frf-ffi` is a **UniFFI** crate (the same surface that
> produces the Swift/Kotlin bindings). flutter_rust_bridge cannot parse a UniFFI crate —
> it errors on the `#[uniffi::export]` surface — so the Dart bindings are generated with
> `uniffi-bindgen-dart` instead (recorded in ADR-003).

To regenerate (after any change to `frf-ffi`):

```sh
cd <workspace-root>
./sdks/dart/build_dart.sh          # requires: cargo install uniffi-bindgen-dart
```

## What gets generated

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `lib/src/rust/frf.dart` | The UniFFI Dart bindings (`library frf;`) — the full API |

The public entry point `lib/frf_dart.dart` re-exports `src/rust/frf.dart`, so consumers
`import 'package:frf_dart/frf_dart.dart';`.

## Rust source

The Rust entry point is `crates/frf-ffi/src/lib.rs`. Types and functions annotated with
`#[uniffi::export]` / `#[derive(uniffi::Object)]` are exposed to Dart: the CRDT functions
(`crdtApplyDelta`, `crdtNewSnapshot`, `crdtSnapshotVersion`) and the transport client
`FrfFfiClient` (`connect` / `publish` / `subscribe` / `ack`, with the `EventCallback`
foreign trait). CRDT bytes cross the boundary as `Uint8List` — the Loro engine is fully
encapsulated in Rust.

## Known limitation (uniffi-bindgen-dart 0.1.3)

The generator currently emits **type-incorrect Dart for async constructors and
foreign-callback methods**. Concretely:

- `FrfFfiClient.connect` is generated returning `FrfFfiClient` instead of
  `Future<FrfFfiClient>`.
- `FrfFfiClient.subscribe` passes the `EventCallback` object where a `u64` handle is
  expected.

So the **synchronous CRDT surface is usable today**, but the **async transport surface
(`connect` / `subscribe`) does not yet type-check**. The generated file is committed and
analyzer-excluded (`analysis_options.yaml`) rather than hand-patched — never edit
generated code. Swift/Kotlin (via UniFFI directly) are unaffected; only the Dart async
codegen is limited. Tracked as a follow-up: re-run `build_dart.sh` when
`uniffi-bindgen-dart` fixes async/callback codegen, or wrap the transport surface in a
hand-written Dart shim over the sync FFI.
